name: Assir
overview: Assir is a male member of the tribe of Levi, specifically identified as a Kohathite. He is uniquely noted as the son of Ebiasaph, situating him within the Levitical genealogies. His role and identity are primarily defined by his lineage within the priestly tribe of Levi.
namesAndTitles: The name Assir means "prisoner" in Hebrew. This is a proper name and is not indicated as being given directly by God. The meaning provides a literal understanding of the name without implying additional spiritual significance.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture explicitly records Assir as the son of Ebiasaph. It is also inferred that Tahath is his father, establishing a generational link within the Levitical family line. Beyond these, no further family relationships are documented in the biblical record.
scriptureSignificance: Assir's significance lies in his place within the Levitical priestly line, specifically as a Kohathite descendant. This lineage is important for understanding the organization and heritage of the Levites, who were set apart for service to God. His mention in 1 Chronicles 6:23 situates him within the genealogical framework that supports the priestly duties and worship practices established under the Mosaic covenant.
